To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel graph-based resource allocation algorithm is proposed and evaluated for V2V communications.

the proposed method provides an optimal solution with low complexity, which is capable of handling the resource allocation problem for V2V sidelink broadcast communication in high vehicular density scenarios, while maintaining the interference at a low level.

we present a resource allocation scheme for V2V communications that: i) is able to allocate resources to vehicles based on their position and ii) takes into account the constraint of time orthogonally of resources allocated within the same cluster.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a graph-based resource allocator which, by exploiting available information on the vehicles geographical position and on the spectrum resources utilization, is capable of allotting resources in a way that the interference generated by repurposing resources is kept under control and, hence, the performance of vehicles is improved.
the problem of allocating resources to vehicles in a V2V broadcast scenario, while ensuring the orthogonality constraint on time resources is fulfilled.
a graph-based resource repurposing scheme for broadcast V2V communications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed method is able to provide optimal solutions in terms of maximizing the number of vehicles that are able to broadcast their signals, while maintaining the interference level at an acceptable level.
the proposed method is able to allocate the same resources to multiple vehicles, thus improving spectrum efficiency, while preventing resource conflicts.
our approach is able to provide the highest achievable throughput for V2V communication networks, while at the same time avoiding conflicts and keeping the interference at a minimum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the graph-based resource allocation approach is a viable solution to avoid interference and resource conflicts in V2V communications.
the presented graph-based resource allocation method provides an optimal solution with a low computational cost and is capable of handling the aforementioned constraints.

the proposed method can be implemented as a standalone algorithm or as part of an eNodeB’s scheduler, providing the eNodeB with a resource allocation scheme capable of avoiding conflicts and minimizing the interference level in the sidelink.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed approach can be used to provide optimal resource allocation in scenarios with a high number of vehicles, which is of paramount importance for future V2X communications.
the proposed approach can be applied to a variety of resource allocation problems where the goal is to maximize the sum-rate of a network.
the proposed approach can be used in practical scenarios, as it is capable of providing a solution in real-time.
